newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-MILAN LOOK FOR MORE SCANDINAVIAN RELIEF.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN LOOK FOR MORE SCANDINAVIAN RELIEF.

text.p: AC Milan, haunted by poor form and injuries, will seek a second dose of Scandinavian relief when they meet Gothenburg in the European Champions' League on Wednesday.

Milan thrashed the Norwegians of Rosenborg 4-0 in their last European outing two weeks ago, sparky striker Marco Simone scoring a hat-trick in the chilly air of Trondheim and Liberian George Weah grabbing a fourth.
Simone, who missed Saturday's 3-0 defeat at Roma through injury, returns to partner the majestic Weah in attack as Milan try to repeat their Norwegian victory.

Gothenburg emphasised their total domination of Swedish football at the weekend by clinching their fourth successive league title with a 6-0 away win at Trelleborg but they have had a miserable run in Europe, losing to Rosenborg and Porto.
Milan started with a shock defeat at home to Porto but put their campaign back on track against Rosenborg, who play Porto at home on Wednesday.
Milan's Uruguayan coach Oscar Tabarez has been obliged to make sweeping changes for the Gothenburg tie.
Dutchman Edgar Davids, Montenegrin Dejan Savicevic and Stefano Eranio are all ruled out by injury while defender Pietro Vierchowod is cup-tied.
Captain Franco Baresi, who played his first game in over six weeks on Saturday, is expected to play against Gothenburg despite being less than 100 percent fit.
In order to provide extra cover for Baresi, Tabarez may move Frenchman Marcel Desailly back to central defence in place of out-of-form Alessandro Costacurta.
Two younger squad members -- 19-year-old Massimo Ambrosini and 20-year-old Tomas Locatelli -- are on standby for midfield berths alongside Demetrio Albertini and Croat Zvonimir Boban.
Boban, suspended on Saturday, said he hoped defeat in Rome would spur the side on in the Swedish west coast city.
"It (the defeat by Roma) wasn't nice to look at, not at all...We'd better show some character and react," he said.

Boban's sentiments were shared by Costacurta, who said: "Thank goodness we now have a cup match. I don't know what exactly is happening at the moment. We're conceding goals that, if not inexplicable, are at least worrying."
Gothenburg are on a domestic high after securing the national league title on Saturday with two matches to spare before winter ends the Swedish season.
Swedish internationals Andreas Andersson and Stefan Pettersson scored two goals each in their 6-0 win, which keeps Gothenburg in next season's Champions' League.
Gothenburg - Thomas Ravelli, Magnus Johansson, Teddy Lucic, Mikael Nilsson, Stefan Landberg, Mikael Martinsson, Hakan Mild, Magnus Erlingmark, Jesper Blomqvist, Stefan Petterson, Andreas Andersson
AC Milan - Sebastiano Rossi, Christian Panucci, Paolo Maldini, Marcel Desailly, Franco Baresi, Tomas Locatelli, Demetrio Albertini, Massimo Ambrosini, Zvonimir Boban, George Weah, Marco Simone
